newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed amid Turkey concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed amid Turkey concerns.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby December dropping late on commercial selling with talk Turkey may turn back shipments of U.S. wheat also mentioned, traders said.
Traders said Cargill Inc and Merrill Lynch Futures each sold nearly two million bushels of December near the close.
Wheat held firm much of the session on an impressive recovery in soybeans and on a short-term technical bounce.
"It was a little technical correction (early gains), a little demand surfaced as U.S. soft red winter became mildly competitive," said Skip Searcy of FIMAT Futures.
But "long term wheat trends remain bearish," he said.
Concerns about the fate of U.S. wheat exports to Turkey apparently stemmed from rumors Turkey may be clamping down on inspections of U.S. wheat cargoes.
"It sounds as if the government is starting some kind of zero-tolerance program," an MGE trader said, adding that the concerns included vomitoxin and TCK smut.
Wheat closed one cent pwer bushel lower to two cents higher, with December down one at $3.98-1/2 and March down 1/2 at $3.91.
Technical indicators in wheat remain bearish.
Traders said the key moving averages (MA) show the market remains poised for further declines with the four-day MA for December closing at $4.01, 18-day at $4.19 and 40-day at $4.28-3/8.
But the short term nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December ended at 21.995 points. The market generally views an RSI of 30 or less as oversold and 20 or less as very oversold.
During Wednesday's session first resistance in December was at $4.03-1/4 a bushel and second resistance at $4.12-3/4. First support was at $3.93-3/4 and second support was at $3.84-1/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 16,000, down from 22,304 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, Smith Barney sold 300 December $3.80 puts at 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 cents, Refco Inc sold 375 December $4.80 puts at 76-1/2 to 77 cents and Paine Webber bought 200 December $4.40 calls at 7/8 cent, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,000, down from 9,037 Tuesday.
